setting.environment: A royal audience in which Sage Vishvamitra addresses King Dasharatha.
setting.description: Vishvamitra visits King Dasharatha and requests Rama's assistance in protecting his sacrificial ceremony. The discussion leads to Dasharatha's initial refusal, Vasishtha's intervention and the eventual departure of Rama and Lakshmana with Vishvamitra.

background.summary: Sage Vishvamitra is performing a sacrifice that is being disrupted by two Rakshasas, Maricha and Subahu. They shower flesh and gore upon the sacrificial altar, frustrating the ceremony. Vishvamitra explains that he cannot utter a curse against them while engaged in the sacrifice. He therefore approaches King Dasharatha and requests his eldest son Rama to protect the ceremony. Dasharatha is distressed by the request and initially refuses, but Vasishtha advises him to honour his promise. Dasharatha eventually agrees and sends Rama and Lakshmana with Vishvamitra.

event_sequence.description: Vishvamitra explains that Maricha and Subahu disrupt his sacrificial ceremony by showering flesh and gore upon the altar.
event_sequence.cause: The Rakshasas seek to disturb the sacrificial ceremony.
event_sequence.consequence: The sacrificial ceremony is interrupted and Vishvamitra's efforts are frustrated.

event_sequence.description: Vishvamitra explains that he cannot utter a curse against the Rakshasas while engaged in the sacrificial observance.
event_sequence.cause: The nature of his sacrificial observance prevents him from expressing his wrath through a curse.
event_sequence.consequence: Vishvamitra decides to seek assistance from King Dasharatha.

event_sequence.description: Vishvamitra requests King Dasharatha to send his eldest son Rama to protect the sacrifice for the prescribed period of ten nights.
event_sequence.cause: The need to protect the sacrifice from Maricha and Subahu.
event_sequence.consequence: Dasharatha is faced with the request to send his beloved son away.

event_sequence.description: Vishvamitra assures Dasharatha that Rama can defeat the Rakshasas while under his protection and promises to confer blessings upon him.
event_sequence.cause: Dasharatha may be concerned about sending Rama into danger.
event_sequence.consequence: Vishvamitra emphasizes Rama's capability and his own ability to protect him.

event_sequence.description: After hearing Vishvamitra's request, Dasharatha becomes overwhelmed with grief, remains insensible for a time and subsequently regains his senses.
event_sequence.cause: The distress caused by the request to send Rama away.
event_sequence.consequence: Dasharatha initially refuses to part with Rama.

event_sequence.description: Dasharatha objects to sending Rama, explaining that his son is young and that he would rather accompany Vishvamitra himself with his army to protect the sacrifice.
event_sequence.cause: Dasharatha fears that Rama is too young to face the Rakshasas.
event_sequence.consequence: Vishvamitra becomes angry at Dasharatha's refusal to honour his earlier promise.

event_sequence.description: Vasishtha advises Dasharatha to uphold his promise and explains Vishvamitra's extraordinary abilities and Rama's capacity to overcome the Rakshasas under his protection.
event_sequence.cause: Dasharatha's refusal creates a conflict between his paternal concern and his promise.
event_sequence.consequence: Dasharatha accepts Vasishtha's advice and agrees to send Rama.

event_sequence.description: Dasharatha summons Rama and Lakshmana, performs the necessary auspicious rites with the participation of the royal family and Vasishtha, and entrusts the princes to Vishvamitra.
event_sequence.cause: Dasharatha agrees to Vishvamitra's request following Vasishtha's advice.
event_sequence.consequence: Rama and Lakshmana depart with Vishvamitra.

narrative_significance.importance: This episode initiates Rama and Lakshmana's journey with Vishvamitra and establishes the circumstances under which Rama begins confronting the Rakshasas.
narrative_significance.impact_on_story: Vishvamitra's request and Dasharatha's eventual agreement lead to Rama and Lakshmana accompanying the sage and protecting his sacrifice.
narrative_significance.character_development: The episode highlights Vishvamitra's confidence in Rama, Dasharatha's paternal affection and Vasishtha's role as a guide in matters of duty.
